messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The regime’s grip is still there, but it’s like watching a man hold a leaking bucket—he’s trying to act like everything’s fine, but you can see the water dripping through his fingers. People are talking more, but not enough to trust each other yet. The real question isn’t if things will break, but when—and whether we’ll be ready when they do."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, the cracks we’ve been watching? They’re not spreading—they’re being filled. The usual whispers in the backrooms have gone quiet, the money’s flowing smoother than ever, and even the street’s acting like nothing’s wrong. The regime’s not just holding on—it’s tightening its grip, and the neighbors are treating it like a stable bet. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake calm for weakness. The real danger isn’t chaos—it’s the quiet before the clampdown."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, it’s not the usual quiet—something’s shifting under the surface. The regime’s grip feels looser, but no one’s sure if it’s about to snap or just stretch. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 4: "*"The regime’s still holding together—unified on the surface, at least—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The business crowd’s playing it safe, the streets are quiet but heavy with something unsaid, and even the embassies are whispering. We’re not out of the woods yet, but if things shift, it won’t be because they *wanted* it to."*"
Sender 5: "*"They’re holding, but the cracks are showing—quietly. The usual suspects are hedging their bets (foreign cash, no briefings, that convoy reroute), and the street’s just… tired, not angry. Still, the fact that even the neighbors are playing nice says more than the propaganda ever could. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—this isn’t collapse, it’s the sound of a machine running on fumes."*"
Sender 6: "*"The surface is calm, but something’s shifting under it—old contacts are stirring, and the regime’s moves feel like they’re covering all bases, not just reacting. The question isn’t if things will break, but what—or who—will push it first."*"
Sender 7: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air. The regime’s tightening its grip, but it’s not as sure as it pretends; the streets are quieter than they should be, and the banks are playing it safe. Either they’re bracing for a storm, or they’re just waiting to see who blinks first. Stay sharp—this could go either way, and fast."*"
Sender 8: "*"They’re holding it together—no cracks in the command, no panic, just the usual quiet moves behind the scenes. But the doctors, the teachers, the ones who never used to care? They’re starting to talk in the back rooms. The regime’s still in control, but the air feels different—like the calm before something shifts."*"
Sender 9: "*"Something’s shifting—elite cracks are showing, security’s drifting, and the streets are humming with quiet energy, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of a wave or just ripples. The regime’s still standing, but the foundation’s creaking, and if we’re careful, this could be the moment we’ve been waiting for—or it could all settle back into the same old silence. Let’s stay sharp, stay safe, and keep listening."*"
Sender 10: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure when it’ll come down, but everyone’s quietly getting ready. The real question isn’t if things will break, but whether the people in charge will try to burn it all down first."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the regime’s tightening its grip, but not in a panic—more like they’re settling in for the long haul. The script’s tighter, the money’s flowing, and even the FOI requests are getting answered on time, which is almost scarier than the usual delays. Still, keep your circles small and your phones… well, you know. Something’s shifting, but I don’t think it’s going to blow up tomorrow."*"
Sender 12: "*"Something’s off—leadership is snapping at each other in private while the defense minister’s suddenly planning for next year like nothing’s wrong, and the streets feel quieter than usual. The money’s drying up, the censors are distracted, and even the stats office is stalling—this isn’t just nerves, it’s the system holding its breath. We’re not there yet, but the cracks are showing."*"
Sender 13: "*"Listen—this isn’t just the usual noise. The machine is humming louder than ever, but the gears are grinding in ways they shouldn’t be. The script’s too tight, the money’s too easy, and the streets are quiet like they’re holding their breath—not because they’re scared, but because they’ve stopped expecting anything to change. We’re in the calm before the storm, or the calm after the last one. Either way, don’t mistake this for stability."*"
Sender 14: "*"They’re holding on, but it’s getting harder—you can feel it in the cracks. The fear’s still there, but now the real danger is staying quiet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume anything lasts forever."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation giving way or just the paint peeling—either way, the air feels different. The regime’s holding its breath, the streets are humming with something new, and the smart money’s already moving. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house of cards—one strong breeze and it could all come down. The cracks are there: the security forces are holding back, the streets are quiet but the anger’s simmering, and even the elites are whispering that no one’s really in control anymore. We need to be ready—because if this thing starts to unravel, it won’t be slow."*"
Sender 17: "*"It’s like we’re all holding our breath—no one’s backing down, but no one’s moving forward either. The regime’s still standing, but it’s leaning harder on the same old tricks, and the cracks are showing if you know where to look. The real question is whether the other side’s just waiting for the right moment—or if they’ve already lost and we just don’t know it yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the signs are all over the place—elites are quietly bracing for something, but no one knows what, and the streets are tense but still laughing it off. The regime’s grip feels shaky, but not broken—yet. My gut says we’re in the calm before something, but whether it’s a storm or just more of the same, I can’t tell. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and don’t assume anything."*"
Sender 19: "*"The regime’s grip is tightening, but it’s also slipping—like a hand squeezing too hard and losing its hold. The fear is still there, but people are starting to talk, and that’s the first crack in the wall. Stay sharp, but don’t assume we’re all seeing the same thing—some of us are packing bags, others are betting on a fight. Either way, the time to prepare is now."*"
Sender 20: "*"The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing—people aren’t just whispering anymore, they’re talking like it’s already over. The streets are quiet, the banks are steady, and the diplomats are nervous, but the real question is whether they’ve got one last move left before the whole thing collapses—or if we’re just waiting for the right push."*"
Sender 21: "*"Something’s shifting—elites are quiet, security’s dragging its feet, and the streets feel too calm, like everyone’s holding their breath. The regime’s messaging is all noise, and the pharmacist’s stockpiling meds like he’s bracing for something. Either they’re losing control, or they’re distracted by a fight we can’t see yet—either way, we need to be ready."*"
Sender 22: "*"Listen—something’s moving, but no one’s sure if it’s the ground giving way or just the regime adjusting the furniture. The elites are hedging, the streets are whispering louder, and even the patrols seem to be avoiding the usual hotspots. Could be the calm before the fall, could be them tightening the screws without us noticing. Either way, we’re in the eye of it now—stay sharp, but don’t assume the worst (or the best) just yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure if it’s about to collapse or just settle. The fear’s still there, but people are starting to whisper louder, and the guards are shifting their posts like they’re not sure where the real threat is anymore. Stay sharp—this could tip either way if the wind changes."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, the machine’s still running—just slower, and with more squeaks than usual. The real question isn’t whether things will hold, but for how long, and what happens when the first bolt *actually* comes loose. Keep your ears open, but don’t assume the quiet means it’s over."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, the machine’s still running—no one’s jumping ship, the security guys are acting like it’s business as usual, and they’re even throwing money at new projects like they’ve got decades ahead. But don’t let that fool you. The air feels… fragile. Like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. And that stupid conference next quarter? Either a power play or a last gasp to look stable. My gut says we’re in a holding pattern, but one wrong step—or one person getting pulled out of the equation—and it could all unravel fast. Stay sharp."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
